title: React Essentials
description: The packages every React app installs, what each one does, and how to keep their versions in sync.

data.text: A React app is assembled from a small set of npm packages: the core library, the DOM renderer, and TypeScript type definitions. Knowing which is which prevents the classic "two copies of React" runtime error.

rows: Components, hooks, and the element model
Renders React into the browser DOM (and server APIs)
TypeScript types for the DOM renderer

data.title: Scaffold and install the core set
data.content: React's official tooling is create-react-app successor Vite via a template.
data.code:
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-app
npm install
npm install react react-dom
npm install -D @types/react @types/react-dom typescript

data.caption: src/main.tsx — the modern entry point

data.text: `react-dom/client` is the React 18+ entry point. When you upgrade React, you must upgrade `react-dom` to the same major version and update the type packages — they are versioned independently and mismatches produce confusing type errors.

data.title: Two copies of React
data.text: If a dependency bundles its own React, hooks throw "Invalid hook call" or "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useState')". Check with `npm ls react` or `npm dedupe`, and declare React as a peerDependency in libraries you publish.

data.title: Detect duplicate React installations
data.code:
npm ls react
# app@1.0.0
# ├── react@18.3.1
# └─┬ my-ui@1.0.0
#   └── react@17.0.2   <-- second copy: widen the library's peer range

terms.definition: The renderer-agnostic core library that defines components, hooks, and elements.
The package that connects React to the browser (and provides react-dom/server).
A dependency the host app must provide; React libraries declare react and react-dom this way.
A development-only wrapper that double-invokes render and effects to surface unsafe code.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Explain why react and react-dom are separate packages and why every React library declares them as peer dependencies rather than bundling them.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: react is the library; react-dom renders it to the DOM.
Type packages live in devDependencies and are versioned separately.
Keep react and react-dom on the same major version.
Duplicate React copies are the usual cause of invalid-hook errors.
data.takeaway: The React package split is a small detail that reveals whether you understand peer dependencies.
